sourceName: Cloudflare Agents documentation (summarized in our own words)

chunks.title: Overview: three clients
chunks.text: Cloudflare Agents client SDK: clients connect to one named instance of an agent (a Durable Object). useAgent (agents/react) = React hook, live WebSocket, state sync, auto-reconnect with backoff. AgentClient (agents/client) = same over WebSocket for any JS runtime (Vue, Svelte, Node, Bun, Deno). agentFetch (agents/client) = one HTTP request without a persistent connection (server-to-server, cron). For chat UIs, useAgentChat (@cloudflare/ai-chat/react) sits on top of useAgent and exposes the AI SDK useChat shape.

chunks.title: Install and wrangler config
chunks.text: Install: npm i agents @cloudflare/ai-chat ai @ai-sdk/react workers-ai-provider. wrangler.jsonc needs a Durable Object binding for the agent class plus a SQLite migration: "durable_objects": {"bindings": [{"name": "ChatAgent", "class_name": "ChatAgent"}]}, "migrations": [{"tag": "v1", "new_sqlite_classes": ["ChatAgent"]}], and "ai": {"binding": "AI"} for Workers AI. The SQLite migration is required because chat history and stream buffers are stored in SQLite.

chunks.title: useAgent connection options
chunks.text: useAgent({ agent: "ChatAgent", name: roomId }). agent = class name, turned into kebab-case in the URL (/agents/chat-agent/<name>); name picks the instance, default "default". Options: host/path (other Worker or custom route; default current origin), query (object or async function, e.g. auth token; cached for cacheTtl, default 5 min, refreshed when queryDeps change and dropped on every disconnect so reconnects get a fresh token), onOpen, onClose, onError, onMessage, onMcpUpdate. Returns state, setState, call, stub, send, close, reconnect; React closes on unmount.

chunks.title: State sync
chunks.text: State sync: agent.state is undefined until the first server message. agent.setState(next) sends state to the agent, which runs onStateChanged() and broadcasts to all connected clients; onStateUpdate(state, source) fires with source "client" (you pushed) or "server" (agent pushed). On reconnect the agent sends current state automatically, no manual re-sync.

chunks.title: RPC with @callable and streaming
chunks.text: RPC: mark agent methods with @callable() to call them from clients: await agent.call("getStats") or typed: useAgent<MyAgent>(...) then agent.stub.getStats(). Inside the same Worker use plain Durable Object RPC instead. @callable({ streaming: true }) methods get a StreamingResponse first arg (stream.send(chunk), stream.end()); the client passes { onChunk, onDone, onError } as the third argument of call(). Errors thrown by the method reject the client promise.

chunks.title: AgentClient, agentFetch and non-React chat
chunks.text: Vanilla: new AgentClient({ agent, name, host }) then client.call("method", [args]); call client.close() when done; supports addEventListener open/close/error/message. agentFetch({ agent, name, host }, init) does one HTTP request (GET or POST with body) when you do not need real-time updates. For an AI SDK chat UI outside React (e.g. Vue useChat from @ai-sdk/vue), pass new WebSocketChatTransport({ agent: client }) from agents/chat/transport.

chunks.title: useAgentChat and AIChatAgent
chunks.text: Client: const agent = useAgent({ agent: "ChatAgent", name: userId }); const { messages, sendMessage, status, stop, clearHistory, setMessages, addToolOutput, addToolApprovalResponse, isStreaming, isRecovering } = useAgentChat({ agent }); sendMessage({ text }). Server: class ChatAgent extends AIChatAgent { async onChatMessage(_onFinish, options) { return streamText({ model, messages: await convertToModelMessages(this.messages), abortSignal: options?.abortSignal }).toUIMessageStreamResponse(); } }. Any AI SDK provider works (Workers AI via createWorkersAI({ binding: this.env.AI }), OpenAI, Anthropic).

chunks.title: Message handling, body and data parts
chunks.text: Messages are AI SDK UIMessage objects; render msg.parts (text, tool, data-*). Per-request data: useAgentChat({ agent, body }) (object or function), read on server as options.body; prepareSendMessagesRequest can add headers. Data parts: write { type: "data-x", id, data } into a createUIMessageStream writer; same type+id updates in place; transient: true sends without storing (read with onData). messageConcurrency on the agent: "queue" (default), "latest", "merge", "drop" or debounce. All clients on the same instance receive the updated messages (multi-tab sync).

chunks.title: Tools: server and client
keywords: เครื่องมือ
chunks.text: Tools use the AI SDK tool() helper. Server tools have execute and run in the agent. Client tools have no execute: handle them in useAgentChat({ onToolCall: async ({ toolCall, addToolOutput }) => addToolOutput({ toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId, output }) }), e.g. browser geolocation. Limit tool loops with stopWhen: stepCountIs(5).

chunks.title: Human-in-the-loop approvals
chunks.text: Approvals: add needsApproval (boolean or async ({ input }) => bool) to a tool; the turn pauses. On the client find parts where getToolPartState(part) === "waiting-approval", get const a = getToolApproval(part), then addToolApprovalResponse({ id: a.id, approved: true|false }) (helpers from @cloudflare/ai-chat/react). Rejecting sets output-denied; to give the model a reason use addToolOutput({ toolCallId, state: "output-error", errorText }).

chunks.title: Resumable streams and cancellation
chunks.text: Resumable streaming is on by default: chunks are buffered in SQLite; if the client disconnects the agent keeps generating and a reconnecting client replays the buffer then continues live. Closing a tab does not cancel the server turn; stop() does. cancelOnClientAbort: true lets the browser own the turn; resume: false disables resuming. Pass options.abortSignal to streamText so cancellation works. chatRecovery config (maxAttempts, noProgressTimeoutMs, onExhausted) handles agent restarts mid-turn.

chunks.title: Persistence and storage
chunks.text: this.messages is loaded from SQLite and saved after every turn. maxPersistedMessages caps stored messages but not model context (use AI SDK pruneMessages() for context). persistMessages(msgs) stores and broadcasts without a reply; saveMessages(msgs or fn) stores and starts a reply after any active turn (good for scheduled messages); waitUntilStable() waits for turns to finish. SQLite rows max 2 MB: big tool outputs are compacted automatically; sanitizeMessageForPersistence() can redact before saving.

chunks.title: Errors, MCP and best practices
keywords: ข้อผิดพลาด
chunks.text: Errors: onError/onClose on useAgent for connection issues (it auto-reconnects); wrap agent.call in try/catch for RPC errors; onError in streaming call options. onMcpUpdate(servers) reports MCP server connection state and tools. Best practices: prefer typed stub calls, rely on automatic reconnect and state replay, tune cacheTtl for expiring tokens, close AgentClient yourself. Wire protocol messages are named CF_AGENT_* (e.g. CF_AGENT_USE_CHAT_REQUEST, CF_AGENT_TOOL_APPROVAL, CF_AGENT_STREAM_RESUME_REQUEST).
